newsitem.title: UK: Five-year dollar deals dominate Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Five-year dollar deals dominate Eurobonds.

text.p: Thursday's primary market was dominated by dollar bonds, with the five-year maturity favoured.
L-Bank and Fannie Mae both issued $500 million five-year deals, although they were tapping into different investor bases with the Fannie Mae deal carrying a call in year two.
In the pipeline is a possible $500 million five-year issue for Japan-guaranteed Japan Development Bank, dealers said.

"JDB is planning a $500 million five-year deal, and the issue is likely to be jointly underwritten by a European and a U.S. bank," a syndicate head said, adding no specific mandate had yet been awarded.
The timing of the issue would depend on how the U.S. Treasury market reacts to U.S. retail sales and producer price data due for release on Friday.
"If PPI data is good for the market, the deal will be launched on Monday, otherwise they will wait until after the release of consumer price data next Tuesday," a dealer at a U.S. bank said.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp was also said to be eyeing the market, but a deal from them was likely to be further away, dealers said.
In Europe, Geberit International issued a 157.5 million mark 10-year junk bond, one of the first such deals outside the U.S. where the market is highly developed.
The deal is expected to be the first of many sub-investment grade high-yielding corporate bonds targeted at European investors, dealers said.
Already in the pipeline is a 150 million mark deal for Exide Holdings Europe SA, which is expected next week.

Elsewhere, Spain announced on Thursday it planned to issue a 2.0 billion Ecu/euro bond. The Spanish treasury said the deal was expected to have a 10-year maturity, and would be announced in 15 to 30 days.
London-based syndicate managers said no further details were known in the market, and no mandate for the issue had yet been awarded.
